newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Malaysia palm oil faces obstacles to growth - bank.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil faces obstacles to growth - bank.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil production targets of 8.8 million by 2000 and 12.1 million by 2010 may be achieved, but growth will be hampered by labour shortages, a study by Dutch agri-bank Rabobank said.

To reach those goals a further 1.5 million hectares of palm needed to be planted, and one avenue open to farmers was to continue relocating plantations from west Malaysia to Sabah and Sarawak, it said in a report on the country's agribusiness.
Some production increases would follow productivity gains arising out of improved farming techniques, mechanisation and mill efficiency.
Labour shortages meant investment in the upstream sector was required.
The processing industry should also relocate some activities to consumer nations to strengthen the foothold that Malaysian companies had already secured.
A number of local firms had already established joint venture refineries in China, Mexico, Egypt, Vietnam and Algeria, the study noted.
"Malaysian companies should internationalize, and some encouragement in this is being received from the government."

World palm oil consumption was expected to continue to rise rapidly. Palm oil was inexpensive relative to other oils, and that made it attractive to countries like China which were seeking to improve dietary intake but had little hard currency to spare.
